title: Store bands on the Canal-area corners
summary: A six-piece band played from an attic over a clothing store to draw customers; Tillman played that corner for years, with a band across at the Phoenix wine store.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Yeah, on the front of town side of the bank. They had a place built like an attic, you know, right up over the front of the store. They used to use a six piece band up there every side of that. That was to draw the people into the store. What did they sell? Sell clothes.
No, it's a furniture store there now, I see on that corner. It's on the downtown corner of Porterson Rapport. Downtown, Front of Town corner.
Yeah. Yeah, I think it's got a furniture store there now.
Isn't there a Silverstein's clothing store still in the city somewhere?
No, I don't think so. They got Rubenstein. Oh, maybe it has one. Yeah.
That place is painted sort of a bluish green color, isn't it? No, it is.

Yeah, they sell some kind of furniture or something. Yeah. Well, man, we played on that corner, I guess, for about five, almost ten years. We used to go to Everside Night and on the object side, on the uptown, uptown, back of town corner, used to have a band used to play there. Had a wine store there, Phoenix wine store. Remember the Phoenix? Yeah, I know that part. Phoenix wine store. That's why you used to take the tin can and go in there and get your can of wine for a nickel, draw it yourself out the bar. I've heard of that. Well, Frank Crump and his daddy had a band on that corner. We were just the opposite one another. There's advertising on Portles and Raport. We'd advertise Silverstone, they'd advertise for Phoenix. What time did you start that? We used to start it around about 630 at night and play a quarter to 10, 10 o'clock, 10 o'clock the ladies. Yeah, pretty good.
I never heard anything like that myself lately.
